name: Ayi (China)
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2010. Change Request 2010-019: rename [nun] Nung -> Anong (阿侬语).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; names the referent language Anong 阿侬语 (p. 1).

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2010. Change Request 2010-020: retire [ayx] Ayi (duplicate of Nung/Anong [nun]); submitted by Eric Johnson, SIL East Asia Group; adopted 2011-05-18.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing about stress. Establishes identity: 'Ayi' is a misreading of 阿侬 (Anong) as 阿依; 'There is no record of any language named "Ayi" spoken by members of the Nu nationality in Chinese literature or in the knowledge of local Nu intellectuals' (p. 2); same language as Nung [nun], to be renamed Anong.

sources.citation: Sun Hongkai. 1988. Notes on Anong, a new language (transl. Fengxiang Li). Linguistics of the Tibeto-Burman Area 11(1): 27-63.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Phonology sections I-IV (pp. 27-34): consonants, finals, III 'Tones' (p. 33: four tones 55/53/31/35 plus a conditioned mid-level variant; 'Tones carry a low functional load'), IV 'Syllables'. No mention of stress, accent or prominence anywhere in the 37-page article (full scanned a full-text search for stress/accent/prominen).
Nothing; page states the entry is retired, merged into Anong [nun] as a duplicate per CR 2010-020; no descriptive references listed (Glottolog lists no grammar, sketch or phonology).

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid page nung1282 'Nung (Myanmar)' [nun], alt. names Anong/Anung/Anu/阿儂語.
sources.note: Nothing; confirms that Anong/Anung is the referent languoid; our source list lists 8 descriptive refs under nung1282 (Sun & Liu 2009 grammar, Sun 2005, Sun 2000, Sun 1988, Thurgood & Li 2007, Thurgood 2010).
